qualitative.gate_3m_moat_note: World leader in leased FPSO vessels with proprietary Fast4Ward hull designs, but structurally fails the capital efficiency hurdle with through-cycle ROCE of only 6-9% due to heavy capital intensity ($1B-$2B+ per vessel) and customer concentration (Petrobras, ExxonMobil).
qualitative.note: Fails Gate 3b (ROIC < 12%, REJECT). Leased FPSO model is highly capital-intensive ($1B-$2B per vessel) with through-cycle ROCE of only 6-9%, below the 12% hurdle. High customer bargaining power from concentrated oil majors (Petrobras, ExxonMobil) limits pricing power.
qualitative.evidence: Directional ROCE historically hovers in the mid-single digits (6% to 9%), reflecting heavy project debt and asset-heavy balance sheet requirements. Concentrated customer base in deepwater basins (Guyana, Brazil) negotiates large-ticket terms, preventing economic rents.
